ownership_reason: Only the gold forms the row sums of the product and writes the rows: it reads the stored entries of the sparse matrix in increasing key order, adds value times the matching row of m to the sums of the current row and writes the sums as a row of the product once the last entry of that row has been read. Hop 1 only creates the zero product and returns it, hop 2 only orders the keys, hop 3 only looks up the values and hop 4 passes everything through; none of them reads the product, so once the gold has written a row that still carries earlier rows' contributions no caller can separate them. The gold's javadoc promises the rows of the product; on the trigger the variant's rows 1 and 2 carry row 0's (and row 1's) terms. The convention that each row of a product is summed from zero over its own terms only is pinned outside the gold: the intact sibling overload OpenMapRealMatrix.multiply(OpenMapRealMatrix) adds every term only to the entry of its own row (out.computeKey(i, j)), and AbstractRealMatrix.multiply and BlockRealMatrix.multiply start each output sum at zero; SparseRealMatrixTest::testMultiply2, ::testPremultiply and ::testExamples (sparse products through the sibling overload) and BlockRealMatrixTest::testMultiply pass.
